en.title: Netflix's November 2026 Slate: From Steampunk Marshals to Royal Romances
en.summary: Get ready for a November packed with new and returning Netflix Original series. The streamer is dropping everything from animated adventures to historical dramas and YA hits.
en.body:
Netflix is gearing up for a massive November 2026, promising a diverse slate of original series designed to captivate a global audience. Whether you're craving high-octane animation, heartwarming romance, or gripping drama, the streamer has something lined up for every binge-watcher.

The month kicks off with a truly unique offering: **Bass X Machina**. Arriving November 3rd, this 6-episode animated series reimagines the story of **Bass Reeves**, the first Black deputy U.S. Marshal, through a steampunk lens. Produced by South Korea's acclaimed Studio Mir, known for **Avatar: The Legend of Korra** and **Devil May Cry**, and helmed by producer **LeSean Thomas**, the series plunges Reeves into a lawless world filled with supernatural threats and war machines. It’s a bold premise that promises stunning visuals and a compelling narrative about justice and sacrifice.

Beyond animation, November 2026 sees the return of fan-favorite dramas and the introduction of fresh concepts. While specific details for many titles remain under wraps, confirmed returning series include **The Empress: Season 3** and **Bros: Season 2**. The **Power** series, a significant franchise for the platform, will also see its entire run made available, likely coinciding with new releases or spin-offs. Newcomers like **The Good Lawyer**, a legal drama, and the YA series **The Body** are also slated, alongside the Australian comedy **Allen (2026)**, which follows a man whose alien encounter from 20 years prior resurfaces.

## What Fans Are Saying

The anticipation for Netflix's November slate is palpable, especially among dedicated fans of its original programming. The return of shows like **The Empress** and **Bros** signals Netflix's commitment to nurturing its popular franchises, a move that typically garners significant fan engagement. The inclusion of **Bass X Machina** also represents an exciting risk, appealing to animation enthusiasts and those interested in historical reimaginings. With a blend of established hits and ambitious new projects, Netflix is clearly aiming to solidify its position as a go-to destination for series television, with the potential for these shows to spark widespread online discussion and fan theories.

## What's Next

As November 2026 approaches, Netflix will undoubtedly reveal more details about its upcoming original series. Keep an eye out for release date announcements for titles like **Misty Green (2026)** and **The Christmas Switch (2026)**, as well as any further information on the highly anticipated **The Boroughs**, produced by the **Stranger Things** creators.

The streamer has you covered with original offerings whether you’re in the mood for a comedy, a thriller, a YA series, or some historical fiction.  November 2026 is all about new and returning Netflix Original series. While we’re seeing some fan-favorite dramas come to Netflix, such as the entire Power series , it’s the return of hit series like The Hunting Wives and The Empress that really has our attention. You can also check out here for the full list of what’s coming to Netflix throughout November .  Bass X Machina Picture Credit: Netflix Coming to Netflix: November 3 A creative spin on the story of real-life hero Bass Reeves, an escaped slave from the 1800s who became the first Black deputy U.S. Marshal, Netflix’s steampunk animated series Bass X Machina comes from one of the industry’s most esteemed teams. The 6-episode series is produced by South Korea’s Studio Mir (the studio behind Avatar: The Legend of Korra and Devil May Cry ) alongside producer LeSean Thomas.  The series sees Reeves as a slick bounty hunter in a lawless world full of supernatural threats, deadly outlaws, and war machines. And as he battles, he knows that every act of justice meant to protect his family could ultimately cost him the very people he’s fighting to save. As another prestige, high-octane adult animation in Netflix’s arsenal, Bass X Machina has positioned itself as the perfect series to watch while we await the long-anticipated Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 .  North of North (Season 2) Picture Credit: Netflix Coming to Netflix: November 5 Prepare for a return to Ice Cove, folks! Canadian comedy North of North  Season 2 is heading to Netflix on November 5. The new season takes place as winter closes in on the tight-knit community, and Siaja has bigger hopes than ever: she wants to prove to her boss, Helen, that she has big ideas and is much more than just someone who just manages the calendar. “There is a lot that’s happening in season two,” Lambe teased to Canadian outlet The Gate in an interview. “This season is beautiful, it’s funny, but it’s also heartbreaking, and the things that mean the most to Siaja are really thrown up in the air, so that never-ending positivity really helps get her through it.” The second season debuted at APTN+ and CBC back September 8th, receiving strong ratings.  Black Doves (Season 2) Picture Credit: Netflix Coming to Netflix: November 5 Almost two years after spy thriller Black Doves debuted on Netflix, Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw are back as Helen and Sam for Season 2.
